land.text: Mahan, one of the three states that 'succeeded' Jin

predecessors.note: Preceded by Jin (Korean state) on the Mahan infobox.

land.text: Baekje's first Cliopatria shape, identical to Mahan's

successors.note: The page: 'Paekche eventually absorbed or conquered all of Mahan by the 5th century'; the Baekje page puts the last annexations in Geunchogo's reign (346-375). Cliopatria hands the whole shape over in 346/347.

capitals.name: Mokji (Cheonan)
capitals.note: Mahan infobox: 'Capital: Mokji'; Mokji 'was centered in Cheonan'. The same page says the Mokji state was defeated by Paekche in the 1st century CE, after which the confederacy's seat is not recorded; the dot is held for the whole life for want of a successor seat.

keyframe_review.note: -91..337, 49,731 km2 (Jeolla, Chungcheong and the Han valley up to 38.35N). The Samhan page describes Mahan as 'Jeolla, Chungcheong, and portions of Gyeonggi'; neither page gives an area. The shape includes the Han-valley statelet of Paekche ('Paekche (Seoul)' is one of the 54 statelets), although the Baekje page has Paekche a kingdom from 18 BCE and 'full-fledged' under Goi (234-286); the drawn Mahan therefore overstates the confederacy from the 3rd century, and the Baekje dossier's start will decide how much. Unverified for those years: page budget.

338..346, the same outline and area as the first shape. Geunchogo's reign began in 346 and he is the king who 'expanded Paekche's territory to the north through war against Goguryeo, while annexing the remaining Mahan societies in the south' (Baekje page); Cliopatria's Baekje row begins in 347 with the same 49,731 km2. The pages date the absorption to the 1st, late 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th centuries (see notes), so 346 is a bridge.

region.text: 'Jeolla, Chungcheong, and portions of Gyeonggi' (Samhan page); 'a tribal grouping in southwestern Korea' (Mahan page)

ledger.note: 91 BCE: the Mahan confederacy of 54 statelets appears in the south-west, with Mokji (Cheonan) at its head. Cliopatria's first year; the page's infobox says 'Establishment: 194 BCE', the Samhan page that they 'formed around the time of the fall of Old Chosŏn' in 108 BCE, and Chinese sources describe Mahan only 'from the 3rd century'.

346: Baekje takes the rest of Mahan. 'King Geunchogo (346-375) expanded Paekche's territory to the north through war against Goguryeo, while annexing the remaining Mahan societies in the south.' No page gives the year of the last annexation; 346 is Geunchogo's first year and Cliopatria's last year for Mahan.

wars.name: Lelang and Daifang against the Han state (246)
wars.outcome: The Han state fell in struggles with Lelang and Daifang; the page does not say what land changed hands.
wars.note: 'The San Guo Zhi recorded the Han state fallen in struggles with the Lelang Commandery' in 246, with Daifang. Mahan is one of the Han (Samhan) in that record; no zone because no page places a result.

wars.name: Baekje's absorption of Mahan

zones.text: Mahan's remaining statelets in the south and the Mokji heartland

wars.outcome: Baekje rose inside Mahan, overthrew the Mokji state and absorbed the confederacy; the last southern societies were annexed in Geunchogo's reign (346-375).
wars.note: The span is the page's own: Goi (234-286) 'became a full-fledged kingdom' and Geunchogo (346-375) annexed 'the remaining Mahan societies'. Other pages: Mokji defeated 'in the 1st century CE' and 'only 20 statelets ... survived until the late 3rd century' (Mahan page), 'By the 4th century, Mahan was fully absorbed' (Samhan page), 'by the 5th century' (Mahan page). No contest event: no page dates a front.

certainty.note: A loose confederacy of 54 statelets with no frontier on any page; the Cliopatria outline is a block of the south-west.

sources.title: Mahan confederacy
sources.note: Identity, infobox (Mokji, 194 BCE, preceded by Jin, succeeded by Paekche), the 54 statelets, Mokji defeated in the 1st century CE, 246 Lelang.

sources.title: Samhan
sources.note: Samhan formed around 108 BCE; Mahan covered 'Jeolla, Chungcheong, and portions of Gyeonggi'; 'By the 4th century, Mahan was fully absorbed into the Paekche kingdom'.

sources.title: Baekje
sources.note: Founding in 18 BCE inside Mahan, Goi (234-286), Geunchogo (346-375) annexing the remaining Mahan societies.

notes: Cliopatria's Mahan shape is carried unchanged -91..346 and the Baekje row (347..) repeats it exactly (49,731 km2), so Cliopatria treats Mahan and Baekje as one handover in 346/347 although the Baekje page has Baekje founded in 18 BCE at Wiryeseong inside Mahan and a 'full-fledged kingdom' under Goi (234-286); the Baekje dossier (jk-02-b) must reconcile the start and the shape. Pages disagree on when Mahan ended: Mokji defeated 'in the 1st century CE' and 'the late 3rd century' (20 statelets left) and 'by the 5th century' (Mahan page, whose infobox also says 'Submission to Paekche: 6th century CE'), 'By the 4th century' (Samhan page), Geunchogo 346-375 (Baekje page); the dossier keeps Cliopatria's 346 at confidence 1. The Mahan page also names the 54 statelets with modern places (Gamhae/Iksan, Mokji/Cheonan, Paekche/Seoul, Mosu/Suwon, Mallo/Boryeong or Gunsan, Bimi/Seocheon, Saro/Hongseong, Wonji/Yeosu, Chori/Goheung) and a King Jun lineage (Cheongju Han clan list: Jun 220-193 BCE, last king Gye 33-17 BCE), which Korean historians reject; neither is used as territory. The three Samhan infoboxes give 'Establishment: 194 BCE', which the pages' own texts contradict; Cliopatria's -91 is kept (see korean-jin notes). Region names: none unresolved. Page budget: 3 pages of 2 (Baekje opened for Mahan's end).
